instruction: CORRECTNESS-lens R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020H.2 at branch feature/wp-scp-022-020h2-regal-sha256, commit 6d248f3. The slice closes TF-020H3-001 by adding Regal binary SHA256 verification to the SCP federation primitive's reusable workflow, mirroring the existing OPA + Conftest pattern. VERIFY EXACTLY: (1) scripts/.tool-versions: now contains 'regal 0.40.0' as a third line. read_tool_version awk filter (policy-check.yml lines 133-147) handles this correctly — verify by tracing: awk -v tool="regal" '$1 == tool {print $2; ...}' against the 3-line file. Edge case: trailing whitespace, blank line at EOF. (2) scripts/scp-policy-check.lock: regal block has linux-x64 / linux-arm64 / darwin-x64 / darwin-arm64 sub-objects each with `asset` + `sha256`. The shape matches OPA's (single-binary, no archive_sha256) NOT Conftest's (archive + binary). Verify against actual Regal release shape: Regal ships as a bare binary, not a tarball — confirm by checking https://github.com/open-policy-agent/regal/releases/tag/v0.40.0 asset list. (3) SHA256 sums in the lockfile: linux-x64=0301464f1b2ea4e2458cec63cdde4557db09bcbe47505a7bbbfe6bf47aeab234, linux-arm64=af9c2e76a6422628eb82cc228e259cf45e48934eb14c24558d8a7302b085fd99, darwin-arm64=84a3685d4064acdcf7cf8d32ca3e92e5ba99d2d217e8ea018d5f249562d1ab8c, darwin-x64=36e20a41743244e50bac95f649153d36c006d26ede4c2aceccd4f52675af36da. Cross-check against the upstream `checksums.txt` at https://github.com/open-policy-agent/regal/releases/download/v0.40.0/checksums.txt — values must be byte-identical. (4) policy-check.yml REGAL_VERSION sourcing: line ~177 changed from hardcoded `REGAL_VERSION="0.40.0"` to `REGAL_VERSION="$(read_tool_version regal)" || emit_infra_failure ...`. Verify the read_tool_version function actually returns "0.40.0" against the new tool-versions file. (5) policy-check.yml REGAL_SHA256: read via `read_lockfile_field regal "${PLATFORM_KEY}" sha256`. Confirm read_lockfile_field python helper (lines 149-171) handles the regal key + the 4 platform keys correctly. Edge case: PLATFORM_KEY=darwin-* on a Linux runner — when does the workflow encounter darwin? Today's `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` means darwin paths are dead code unless someone runs it on a self-hosted Mac. Document or verify this assumption. (6) policy-check.yml resolve_regal() function: structurally compare against resolve_opa(). The differences should be name-substitutions only (REGAL→OPA, regal→opa, REGAL_REPO→OPA_REPO, REGAL_ASSET→OPA_ASSET, REGAL_SHA256→OPA_SHA256, vendor/regal→vendor/opa). Any non-mechanical divergence is a finding. (7) policy-check.yml curl block replacement: the old block at lines 273-275 (curl, chmod, smoke test) is replaced with `REGAL_SOURCE="$(resolve_regal)" || emit_infra_failure ...; cp ...; chmod +x; <smoke test>`. Verify the smoke-test invocation is preserved (defense-in-depth against SHA-passing-but-corrupt binary). (8) PATH ordering: BIN_DIR is appended to GITHUB_PATH at line ~277. Subsequent steps that invoke `regal lint ...` (line ~410) resolve against this PATH. Verify the regal binary is actually at BIN_DIR/regal post-cp (not a different path). (9) Shell quoting: any unquoted variable expansion in the new resolve_regal block could break if PLATFORM_KEY or REGAL_ASSET contains spaces (they don't today, but the pattern matters). (10) STATUS.md edits: Open scheduled follow-ups table no longer contains the TF-020H3-001 row; Tracked-forward items from 020H part 3 marks TF-020H3-001 closed. Verify both edits are syntactically correct Markdown (table rows balanced, etc.). (11) DISPATCH-NOTE.md — every claim about the actual diff state matches HEAD on the branch. (12) Are there any code paths or workflow steps that USED Regal but were not updated? Specifically: lib/policy_check_invocation.sh, scripts/scp-policy-check, conflict-gate.yml — do any of these reference Regal? If yes, they may also need verification updates. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON. NEVER recommend descoping.
